clue.text: Capital issue to secure in advance

parts.note: fore means at the front, ahead
to lock something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A finance clue: a capital issue, shares offered to raise money, secured ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital issue' reads as finance, but the capital is the head and the issue is what grows from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lock of hair growing from the front of the head is something the head puts out, so it is cryptically a head's product.

clue.text: Legitimate target in hoopla, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone it is acceptable to attack or criticise

definitions.note: an example of the second sense
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a game played at a funfair, of which hoopla, tossing rings over prizes, is one

explanation.surface: The prizes at a ring-toss stall are there to be aimed at.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoopla is a British fairground game of throwing rings over prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names anyone open to attack or ridicule, from game animals one may lawfully hunt.

clue.text: Engineers effective in providing support

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a law in force is effective

explanation.surface: Army engineers prove their worth by shoring something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce a structure or argument is to strengthen it by adding further backing.

clue.text: Security device incorporated in wall at Chequers

indicators.note: incorporated in means contained inside, so the letters sit within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the word break

explanation.surface: A security feature is built into the wall of the Prime Minister's country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country residence.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a bar or catch that fastens a door or gate shut.

clue.text: A plant to force? My mistake

indicators.note: a mistake garbles things, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener admits they were wrong to try to force a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: To force a plant is to make it grow early under cover, which suits the gardening scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfrey is a hairy-leaved herb of the borage family, long grown in gardens for medicine.

clue.text: A secondary highway overseas

parts.note: taken as written
British minor routes are classed B, below the main class of route

explanation.surface: A minor road is described as leading abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded: A roads are main routes, B roads are the lesser ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe being in or going to a foreign country across the sea.

clue.text: Having two parties involved at Liberal assembly

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together anew, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Two political parties are both involved at a Liberal Party gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral talks or treaties are between two sides, each side being one of the pair.

clue.text: Instrument of gold with silver mounting on point

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so one part sits over the next

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means climbing upward, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A precious instrument of gold, with silver set on its tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipe organ is a keyboard instrument, the largest found in churches and concert halls.

clue.text: Dislike of French cricket

parts.note: de is French for of
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Someone's distaste for French cricket, a children's bat-and-ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: French cricket is a simple garden game; here French and cricket are split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to dislike intensely, a strong form of the same verb.

clue.text: Devalues pound with support from those in debt

indicators.note: in a down clue support comes from below, so the next part goes underneath

parts.note: L is the pound sign, from Latin libra
owers are people who owe

explanation.surface: Sterling is weakened when debtors prop it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower something's worth is to reduce its value, so it describes devaluing.

clue.text: I do it free it's natural

definitions.note: a noun here, an old word for a simple-minded person

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and can rearrange

parts.note: the three short words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone declares that doing a thing freely comes naturally to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'natural' looks like an adjective, but it is the old noun for a person born simple-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage a natural was a person of low intelligence from birth, a fool.

clue.text: Acting in State fair beamed from satellite

definitions.note: the clue text looks garbled in the scan; moonlight is to do a second job on the side

parts.note: the Moon is Earth's natural satellite
fair hair or skin is light in colour

explanation.surface: Someone performs at a state fair under the glow of the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned clue reads oddly; the satellite and fair supply the two halves, read in reverse order of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To moonlight is to take secret extra work, so the definition points to working or acting outside one's main post.

clue.text: Amount, say, of donation exciting suspicion ?

definitions.text: Amount, say, of donation exciting suspicion

parts.note: surface reading: the size of a gift; setter's reading: 'a mount', a steed given as a present
the proverb warns against looking such a present in the mouth, so suspicion of it is frowned on

explanation.surface: Someone questions how large a donation was, and the sum looks suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amount, say' splits as 'a mount', a horse; the proverb says never to look a gift one in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a present whose quality one should not inspect, from checking a horse's teeth for age.

clue.text: Backward group without books in, temporary accommodation

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one part sits round another
going backward means the word for group is read from its end

parts.note: a set is a group of things
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A backward group lacking books ends up in makeshift lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvas shelters are pitched for a short stay and taken down again, so they are short-term lodging.

clue.text: Messenger happy to pocket copper

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: merry means cheerful
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A cheerful courier quietly keeps some small change.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman myth Mercury was the winged messenger of the gods, matching the Greek Hermes.

clue.text: Averse to rescinding testament

definitions.meaning: first meaning: reluctant, not wanting to

definitions.note: a cryptic sense: un-willing, undoing a will

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to revoking a will.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is split as un-willing: removing what one has willed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reluctant or disinclined is opposed in mind, which is what being averse means.

clue.text: Scattered from extremes of terror in all directions

indicators.note: in places one part inside another

parts.note: the four compass points south, east, west and north

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of terror

explanation.surface: People flee a terror and are flung every which way.
explanation.definitionFit: Things strewn have been spread loosely over an area, which is what scattered describes.

clue.text: Motto for guard on express, perhaps

parts.note: a watch is a guard or lookout
to word something is to express it, perhaps; on places it after

explanation.surface: A guard on an express train needs a slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' looks like a fast train; it is the verb to put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchword is a slogan or rallying principle, the same as a guiding motto.

clue.text: Quicker off the mark in the theatre

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more prompt, read as a comparative adjective

definitions.note: the second sense, a person who works in the theatre
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the person offstage who feeds actors forgotten lines

explanation.surface: Someone reacts faster in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre prompter cues actors with lines; read as a comparative, the word means more punctual.

clue.text: Echoing cry — it may indicate bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a call whose name imitates its own sound
second meaning: the lapwing, named after that call

explanation.surface: A cry rings out and echoes, suggesting a bird nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Echoing' here means imitative: the word copies the sound it names, so the call and the bird share it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing is called after its plaintive two-note call, an imitative name used for both the call and the bird.

clue.text: Work  in that headgear?

indicators.note: in places one word within another

parts.note: taken as written
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they should go to work in that hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall silk cylindrical hat, worn with formal dress, is a kind of headgear.

clue.text: Cover used by gunner, possibly

parts.note: surface reading: shelter for an artillery soldier under fire; setter's reading: a sheath for a pistol
signals that gunner is only one kind of user, a gunslinger rather than a soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier at the guns takes cover from enemy fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests protection in battle; it is a leather case for a handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunman's pistol rides in a leather case on the belt, a cover for the weapon itself.

clue.text: Precarious situation for those at play

indicators.note: letters at play move about freely and rearrange

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A tricky situation arises for actors performing on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an uncomfortable position of pressure or responsibility, where one is exposed to criticism.

clue.text: Girl discarded is ruined

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
to shed is to cast off

explanation.surface: A jilted girl is left devastated.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, hopes or chances that are dished have been spoiled or wrecked completely.

clue.text: I am to lead exercises introducing student project

definitions.note: a verb here: to propel forward

indicators.note: to lead means to go first, so this piece opens the answer

parts.note: contracted to I'm
PE is physical education, school exercises
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A teacher announces they will lead the exercises for a student's project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a noun for a school task; it is the verb, to throw forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To project something is to drive or propel it forward, which is what impelling does.

clue.text: Fay left in danger

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian legend, and fay is an old word for a fairy
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A girl called Fay has been left in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: Fay looks like a girl's name, but it is the old word for a fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril means exposure to serious risk or harm, so it is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Look closely at shirt taken in with artificial fabric

indicators.note: something taken in is held within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
a T is a T-shirt
sham means fake

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a shirt that has been altered, finding the fabric synthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artificial fabric' looks like the definition, but artificial is wordplay; the fabric alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a heavy corded ribbon, or a thick woollen cloth once used for overcoats.

clue.text: Steal toy with missing head

indicators.note: missing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to trifle with something is to toy with it

explanation.surface: A doll has been stolen and its head is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to search through and plunder, taking things that are not yours.

clue.text: Wine order for me, I gather

indicators.note: to order things is to put them into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a bottle has been ordered for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermitage is a celebrated red or white wine from a hill in France's northern Rhône valley.

clue.text: Money advanced for empty apartment

parts.note: a flat is the British word for an apartment
empty means nothing, the zero O

explanation.surface: A deposit is paid in advance for a vacant apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: No word marks the insertion: the empty flat is read as a flat with nothing inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash float is a sum provided up front, such as change for a till at the start of trading.

clue.text: Pull with great effort, entering river in flood

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to lug is to haul something heavy

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to haul a load into a river that is in flood.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is an overwhelming flow of water, an inundation such as Noah's.

clue.text: One present given in returning thanks to nurse

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you
a tender is one who tends or looks after someone

explanation.surface: A gift is handed over with thanks to a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift; it means being there.
explanation.definitionFit: An attender is someone who turns up and is there at a meeting or service, physically on hand.
